note: Scripture source: the Indian Revised Version (IRV Hindi, CC BY-SA 4.0), fetched as USX from the ebible mirror (gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/hin_irv/usx), all 66 books. Every mined span was sliced from that text by script, never typed. Translators also had an English-phrase search over the whole Bible (ASV text from pythonbible) keyed to the same verse ids, so uncited quotations were looked up too.

Chapter 3 (The Golden Key of Prayer) reuses the shipped Hindi sermon the-golden-key-of-prayer.hi verbatim — the English book chapter and the English sermon are the same text (one hyphenation apart) — with its straight quotation marks mapped position-for-position onto the book's curly ones. Its references here are that sermon's notes, re-labelled chapter_order 3.

Derived by measurement: a row is mined only when a 6+ character quoted segment in that block is a byte substring of the cited IRV verse (or a 25+ character common run), AND the translator reported the quotation as verbatim. adapted (person/grammar changed), self (IRV differs), and 13 verbatim claims the measurement could not confirm are self_rendered. Unquoted echoes/allusions are not recorded.

KJV/IRV divergences an editor should see (details in the translators' reports, summarised): Job 23:4 IRV has no 'fill my mouth with arguments' (ch04's central image — IRV quoted, Spurgeon's phrase kept as his own); Ps 5:3 no 'direct my prayer … look up'; 2 Cor 1:12 IRV पवित्रता where the sermon argues from KJV 'simplicity' (ch11); 2 Cor 1:10 IRV has no present 'doth deliver'; Ps 141:5 IRV lacks 'in their calamities' (ch10, self-rendered ×3, identical each time); Ps 37:3 no 'verily thou shalt be fed' (ch12); Phil 4:6 'be presented' vs 'made known'; Jas 4:5 and 2 Pet 1:20 read differently in the IRV (ch05, self-rendered); Hos 14:2 no 'calves of our lips'; Prov 30:28 lizard, not spider; Isa 45:11 questions, not invitation (ch09).

Places a translator departed from the IRV's exact wording to keep Spurgeon's point, all recorded self_rendered, not mined: Luke 23:42 'हे प्रभु' for the IRV's Jesus (ch05); Jonah 1:6 परमेश्वर for the IRV's देवता (ch09); 1 Thess 5:12 जानें for मानो (ch10).

Conventions: curly quotation marks mirror the English per chapter, including its unbalanced counts. ch08's English uses straight ASCII quotes throughout (the only chapter that does); its 86 quotation marks are rendered as curly “ ” so the edition is one style, its 27 apostrophes vanish in Hindi, and 12 straight quotes that stand where the source lost an em dash are rendered —. Congregation तुम, God तू; 'mercy seat' दया का सिंहासन (the ark's lid, where meant, प्रायश्चित्त का ढकना); throne of grace अनुग्रह का सिंहासन; conversion मन-फिराव; supplication विनती (IRV spelling; बिनती normalised). Chapter titles pinned up front so cross-references between sermons agree. Section numerals I., II., III. kept as ch03 (the shipped sermon) has them.

ENGLISH SOURCE defects found and NOT repaired here (the Hindi mirrors each unless noted): ch02 sections numbered II, II, III, IV; ch06 block 6 'irrespective of character' almost certainly lost a 'not'; ch07 'mourning and complaining' (probably 'murmuring' — the translator rendered murmuring, a silent correction a reviewer should know of); ch07 block 50 garbled opening; ch08 whole chapter in straight ASCII quotes with lost em dashes; ch09 '1 throw down the gauntlet' (OCR for I — the stray digit is not carried); ch10 'before the Truth of God' (throne?), 'royal social worker' (almoner?); ch11 'byprayer', 'censor' for censer; ch12 'kno wn'; ch13 'beasthis', 'Sa vior'. Several chapters split one sentence across two paragraphs (ch05 34/35 and 42/43, ch06 six places, ch07 21/22 and 53/54, ch13 24/25); the Hindi keeps the tag split. Spurgeon's own slips kept as preached: Solomon for David (1 Chr 16:3), Moses for Joshua (Josh 7:9), Peniel for Bethel (Hos 12:4), Michael in Dan 10, Daniel praying 'seven times a day'.
Content judgement flagged, not changed: ch02 keeps Spurgeon's anti-Catholic lines ('the harlot Rome', 'the papal power') as he preached them.
